fact: 1929年12月国大党拉合尔年会上，甘地先提出要求英国在两年内给予自治领地位的决议，后妥协为一年；全印国大党委员会以118票对45票通过。苏巴斯·钱德拉·鲍斯在公开会议上提出要求与英国完全决裂的修正案，被以1350票对973票否决，决议全文通过。12月31日午夜，主席贾瓦哈拉尔·尼赫鲁在拉维河畔升起三色旗，宣读包含「准备拒缴赋税」的独立誓词；172名中央与省立法机构议员为此辞职。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Purna Swaraj（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: In December 1929, Congress session was held in Lahore and Mahatma Gandhi proposed a resolution that called for the British to grant dominion status to India within two years. ... The All India Congress Committee voted 118 to 45 in its favour ... The amendment was rejected, by 1350 to 973, and the resolution was fully adopted. ... At midnight on New Year's Eve, President Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the tricolour flag of India upon the banks of the Ravi in Lahore ... One hundred seventy-two Indian members of central and provincial legislatures resigned in support of the resolution

fact: 1930年1月26日，《独立宣言》（Purna Swaraj）正式颁布，国大党号召全国以该日为「独立日」。宣言为一份约750词的文稿，无宪法结构，更像宣言书，宣称英国在印度的统治「不仅剥夺了印度人民的自由，而且建立在剥削群众之上，在经济、政治、文化、精神上毁坏了印度」，因此「印度必须切断与英国的联系，实现Purna Swaraj即完全独立」。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Purna Swaraj（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The Declaration of Independence was officially promulgated on 26 January 1930. ... The resolution was a short 750-word document; it does not have a legal/constitutional structure – instead, it reads more like a manifesto.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Salt March（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The Indian National Congress, led by Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru, publicly issued the Declaration of Sovereignty and Self-rule, or Purna Swaraj, on 26 January 1930.

fact: 1930年3月2日，甘地致信总督欧文，提出11项要求（包括降低土地税、削减军费、对外国布匹征收关税、废除盐税），并表示若要求不被接受将于本月11日起违反食盐法。3月12日，甘地率78名志愿者从萨巴尔马蒂修行地出发，24天步行约385—387公里（240英里）抵达丹迪；4月6日上午8时30分，他自海边泥滩取起一块天然盐，公开违反食盐法，随即引发全国性的大规模违法运动。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Salt March（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The 24-day march (padayatra) lasted from 12 March 1930 to 6 April 1930 as a direct action campaign of tax resistance and nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly. ... Gandhi started this march with 78 of his trusted volunteers. ... The march spanned 387 kilometres (240 mi), from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi ... When Gandhi broke the British Raj salt laws at 8:30 am on 6 April 1930, it sparked large-scale acts of civil disobedience against the salt laws by millions of Indians.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Salt March（镜像 us-wikipedia.com），Preparing to march 小节
sources.quote: On 2 March 1930 Gandhi wrote to the Viceroy, Lord Irwin, offering to stop the march if Irwin met eleven demands, including reduction of land revenue assessments, cutting military spending, imposing a tariff on foreign cloth, and abolishing the salt tax.

fact: 1930年5月4日，甘地致信总督欧文，说明他将前往达拉萨纳盐场；当晚至5月5日凌晨零时45分，苏拉特地区法官率警官与二十余名武装警员在卡拉迪营地将其逮捕。逮捕依据是1827年第25号条例（Regulation XXV of 1827），该条例允许当局自行决定对从事「非法活动」者实施监视与羁押；因此没有审判、没有判决、也没有固定刑期，关押期限「由政府的意愿决定」，甘地被押往浦那耶拉瓦达中央监狱。

sources.title: Mahatma Gandhi 研究网站（mkgandhi.org），Viceroy's Attitude
sources.quote: It was at length decided that Gandhi should be apprehended under Regulation XXV of 1927 which allowed persons engaged in unlawful activities to be placed under surveillance at the discretion of the authorities. ... 'Whereas the Government view with alarm the activities of Mr. M.K. Gandhi, they direct that he should be placed under restraint under Regulation 25 of 1827 and suffer imprisonment during the pleasure of the Government and be immediately removed to the Yeravda Central Jail'.

sources.title: A Pinch of Salt Rocks an Empire（Gandhi Ashram Sevagram）
sources.quote: There was no trial, no sentence and no fixed term of imprisonment. Gandhiji was to be held in prison for as long as the government thought it necessary.

fact: 1930年5月21日，约2500名非暴力志愿者在萨罗吉尼·奈都（Sarojini Naidu）与毛拉纳·阿扎德带领下向达拉萨纳盐场推进，守卫盐场的是约400名警察（含6名英国官员）。志愿者试图拉开设在盐田外围的铁丝网时，警察发起冲锋并以警棍殴打；志愿者按事前命令不抵抗、不举手遮挡。据美国记者韦布·米勒（Webb Miller）现场统计，当场2人死亡、320人受伤，他随后在医院写道「数了320名伤者，许多人颅骨骨折仍昏迷，另有人在腹部与睾丸被踢后痛苦扭动……数十人数小时未获治疗，两人已经死亡」。此事经国际媒体报道，成为1930年最受关注的殖民暴力事件之一。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Dharasana Satyagraha（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: Date 21 May 1930 ... Strength 2,500 ... 400 (including 6 British officials) ... Casualties and losses: 2 dead, 320 wounded (according to Webb Miller) ... Miller later wrote that he went to the hospital where the wounded were being treated, and "counted 320 injured, many still insensible with fractured skulls, others writhing in agony from kicks in the testicles and stomach....Scores of the injured had received no treatment for hours and two had died."

fact: 达拉萨纳事件后，总督欧文在致国王乔治五世的信中写道：「陛下想必已读到关于达拉萨纳盐仓激烈战斗的记述，想必觉得有趣。警察在很长时间内努力克制不采取行动。一段时间后这已不可能，他们不得不采取更严厉的手段。许多人因此受了轻伤。」前立法议会议长维塔尔巴伊·帕特尔在旁观后说：「与英帝国和解的一切希望永远失去了。我可以理解任何政府拘押并惩罚违法者，但我无法理解一个自称文明的政府，会如此野蛮残酷地对待非暴力、不抵抗的人。」这两段引文构成本包记录殖民暴力的核心证据：一方是受害者的现场统计，另一方是殖民当局对同一事件的自我表述。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Dharasana Satyagraha（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: All hope of reconciling India with the British Empire is lost forever. I can understand any government's taking people into custody and punishing them for breaches of the law, but I cannot understand how any government that calls itself civilized could deal as savagely and brutally with non-violent, unresisting men as the British have this morning.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Dharasana Satyagraha（镜像 us-wikipedia.com），Irwin 致乔治五世信
sources.quote: Your Majesty can hardly fail to have read with amusement the accounts of the severe battles for the Salt Depot in Dharasana. The police for a long time tried to refrain from action. After a time this became impossible, and they had to resort to sterner methods. A good many people suffered minor injuries in consequence.

fact: 1930年6月30日，政府逮捕代理主席莫蒂拉尔·尼赫鲁，并宣布国大党工作委员会为非法组织；数千人入狱。至7月，依《新闻条例》查封67家民族主义报纸与约55家印刷所，纳瓦吉万印刷所被查封，《青年印度》与《纳瓦吉万》改以油印方式出版。政府同时大量使用条例统治，监狱人满为患，部分被押者被关入铁丝网围场。

sources.title: Mahatma Gandhi 研究网站（mkgandhi.org），Salt Satyagraha and Dandi March
sources.quote: On June 30, the Government arrested Pandit Motilal Nehru, the acting president, and declared the Working Committee of the Congress as an unlawful association. Thousands of people were jailed. Government by ordinances went on apace. By July, 67 nationalist newspapers and about 55 printing-presses had been shut down under the Press Ordinance. The Navajivan Press was seized and Young India and Navajivan began to appear in cyclostyle.

fact: 1930年11月12日，第一次圆桌会议在伦敦上议院皇家画廊由国王乔治五世正式开幕，由英国首相主持，会期至1931年1月。与会者包括英国八个政党的16名代表、来自英属印度的58名政治领袖与土邦的16名代表，印度方面共74人，其中有穆斯林联盟的阿迦汗三世与真纳、锡克代表、以及代表「不可接触者」的安贝德卡。国大党与印度工商界领袖拒绝出席，包括甘地在内的许多人因参与不服从运动而在狱中；抵制使会议注定失败。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Round Table Conferences (India)（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The Round Table Conference officially inaugurated by George V on November 12, 1930 at Royal Gallery House of Lords in London and chaired by the Prime Minister. ... However, the Indian National Congress, along with Indian business leaders, kept away from the conference. ... Many of them, including Gandhi, were in jail for their participation in Civil Disobedience Movement. ... Their boycott doomed the conference to failure. ... There were fifty-eight political leaders from British India and sixteen delegates from the princely states.

fact: 食盐税率为每maund（约82磅）1卢比4安那。该税1915—1916年为每maund 1卢比，1921—22年升至1卢比4安那，1929年被降回1卢比，1930年又恢复至1卢比4安那——即1930年食盐税实际翻了一倍，并在1931年拟再加征25%至1卢比9安那。盐税约占英属印度税收的8.2%，对最贫困人口的伤害最大；1882年《食盐法》把盐的制造与流通限定在政府盐仓，违反者构成刑事犯罪，即使沿海居民可自行晒盐也被迫向政府购买。

sources.title: 印度议会史料（Council of State Debates, 27 November 1931）Lala Jagdish Prasad 发言
sources.quote: As you know, it is subject to a duty of Rs. 1-4-0 a maund at present. I understand that in 1915 and 1916 the duty on salt was Re. 1 a maund. Then in 1921-22 it was increased to Rs. 1-4-0 a maund. ... in 1929 this tax was reduced to Re. 1 a maund. In 1930, however, the duty was again raised to Rs. 1-4-0 a maund and was retained at that level in the current year.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Salt March（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The 1882 Salt Act gave the British a monopoly on the collection and manufacture of salt, limiting its handling to government salt depots and levying a salt tax. ... Violation of the Salt Act was a criminal offence. ... The salt tax represented 8.2% of the British Raj tax revenue, and hurt the poorest Indians the most significantly.

fact: 抵制英货在1930年秋产生可量化的经济效果：棉布进口降至上一年同期的三分之一至四分之一，香烟进口值降至原来的六分之一；孟买16家英资纱厂关闭，而已作承诺的印度纱厂改为双班生产，约113家纱厂签署声明承诺不生产18支以下的粗纱以避免与土布竞争。土布（khaddar）产量从63万码（lakh yards）升至113万码，卡迪商店从1929年的384家增至1930年底的600家；全印纺纱者协会的活动覆盖约6494个村庄，为约13.99万名纺纱者、1.14万名织工与1006名梳理工提供工作。

sources.title: MAHATMA, Volume 3 (1930-1934)，引自 mkgandhi.org 汇编
sources.quote: By the autumn of 1930 imports of cotton piecegoods had went down to between a third and a fourth of what they were in the same months of the previous year. The cigarettes had fallen in value to a sixth of the old figure. Sixteen British-owned mills in Bombay had been closed down. On the other hand, the Indian-owned mills which had given the pledge were working double shifts. About 113 mills signed declaration ... from 63 lakhs of yards to 113 lakhs of yards. The total number of khadi stores at the end of 1930 was 600, as against 384 in 1929.

fact: 1930年殖民地的两条法律工具决定了参与者的风险结构：一，1882年《食盐法》把盐的制造与流通限定于政府盐仓并征收盐税，违反盐法构成刑事犯罪，可被起诉、判刑；二，1827年第25号条例（Regulation XXV of 1827）授权当局对从事「非法活动」者自行决定实施监视与羁押，无需审判、无固定刑期。前者制造了大量「刑事被告」，后者使甘地这样的核心人物被无限期关押而不进入司法程序。对普通参与者，前者意味着可预期的短期刑期与案底，后者意味着不可预期的长期羁押。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Salt March（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: The 1882 Salt Act gave the British a monopoly on the collection and manufacture of salt, limiting its handling to government salt depots and levying a salt tax. ... Violation of the Salt Act was a criminal offence.

sources.title: Mahatma Gandhi 研究网站（mkgandhi.org），Viceroy's Attitude
sources.quote: It was at length decided that Gandhi should be apprehended under Regulation XXV of 1927 which allowed persons engaged in unlawful activities to be placed under surveillance at the discretion of the authorities. By this means it was expected that the excitement, anger, agitation and demonstrations engendered by a public trial would be avoided.

fact: 至1930年底，因食盐不服从运动被捕者超过6万人；政府以条例统治，查封报纸与印刷所，宣布国大党工作委员会为非法组织。被捕者中绝大多数是普通志愿者与农民，而非领袖；监狱为容纳政治犯而提前释放刑事犯，仍不敷使用。这一规模意味着「被捕」在1930年的印度是一种可预期的日常风险，而不是例外事件。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Salt March（镜像 us-wikipedia.com）
sources.quote: Although over 60,000 Indians were jailed as a result of the Salt Satyagraha, the British did not make immediate major concessions. ... In reaction, the British government arrested over sixty thousand people by the end of the month.

sources.title: MAHATMA, Volume 3 (1930-1934)
sources.quote: The criminals were released to make room for the political prisoners, but even so the jails were overcrowded and many were herded into barbed-wire enclosures.

fact: 1927年3月通过的《货币法》修正案（Ratio Bill）把卢比对英镑的比率法定为1卢比＝1先令6便士（约15卢比兑1英镑），比一战前的1先令4便士升值约12%。这一比价在1927—1931年间靠通缩政策维持：熔化银币而不相应增加纸币发行。1931年9月英国放弃金本位后，印度也脱离金本位，卢比改为钉住英镑，仍维持1先令6便士；财政部长乔治·舒斯特曾提议让卢比浮动，被伦敦否决。

sources.title: Feinstein, Temin & Toniolo, The World Economy Between the World Wars, Ch.8（India within the Sterling Area）
sources.quote: in 1927 legislation was passed to fix the exchange rate to the pound at 1s 6d (a 12 percent appreciation over the already overvalued British currency). This parity was defended in 1927–1931 by way of deflationary monetary policies. These were carried out by melting down silver coins without proportionally increasing paper circulation ... When the pound was taken off gold, the government of India hoped to be able to seize the opportunity for an adjustment of the pound-rupee exchange rate. ... The rupee remained pegged to the pound at the 1927 rate

sources.title: NBER, The Impact of the World Economic Depression on the International Gold Standard, 1929-1931
sources.quote: The Currency Act of 1927 placed upon the government the obligation to purchase all gold presented to the mints in India at a fixed price of Rs. 21-3-10 per tola, corresponding to a sterling parity of 1 s.6 d. per rupee.

fact: 为维持1先令6便士的比价，印度在1930年代初实行紧缩：银行利率至1932年7月前一直为7%，此后降至4%；政府削减开支，公共工程、公共卫生、教育与灌溉支出被压缩，几乎未以公共工程缓解失业。1931年英镑贬值后印度金价上涨，农村家庭持有的黄金大量流出，被称为「黄金的贱卖」（distress sale），这笔流出与持续通缩一起支撑了卢比汇率，也使印度得以支付对伦敦的巨额外债利息。

sources.title: Feinstein, Temin & Toniolo, The World Economy Between the World Wars, Ch.8
sources.quote: A tight monetary policy (the bank rate was 7 percent until July 1932 and 4 percent thereafter) was coupled with cuts in government expenditure. In particular, little was done to reduce unemployment by way of public works, while expenditure on public health, education, and irrigation was curtailed. ... "A large part of the hoarded gold in India, including household possessions of gold in rural India, started to flow out of the country, a process that came to be known as 'distress sale' of gold,"

fact: 自1920年代中期起，殖民政府对钢铁、纺织、糖、纸与火柴等主要产业给予「区别性保护」关税，这是对英国工业利益的重大让步。到1930年代末，印度纱厂已占国内匹头市场的三分之二；工业开始从西印度老工业区向外扩散，马尔瓦里人与切蒂亚尔人等商人社群首次投资制造业。但保护的效果受政府财政紧缩约束，1930年代的萧条中政府「束手无策」。这条「关税保护＋民族主义消费」的内向型增长路径一直延续到1980年代。

sources.title: Cambridge, A Concise History of Modern India, 第6章 The crisis of the colonial order, 1919–1939
sources.quote: Responding to the increasing importance of India's manufacturing industry ... the colonial government ... abandoned its long-standing solicitude for the interests of British industry. From the mid-1920s a measure of 'discriminating protection' was granted to such major industries as iron and steel, textiles, sugar, paper, and matches. ... By the late 1930s Indian mills had secured up to two-thirds of the domestic market for piece-goods.

fact: 1930年抵制英货使印度纱厂主成为直接受益者：加尔各答的《印度纺织杂志》（Indian Textile Journal）称「多亏甘地先生发起的运动，纺织业出现了彻底而可喜的变化……对土布的需求使原本堆满数十万货值的仓库如今空空如也」，艾哈迈达巴德的calico纱厂已由双班改为23小时开工，新商业纱厂开始双班；孟买的新城、芬利、阿波罗与雅各布·沙逊纱厂计划开夜班，「以满足对孟买纱厂产品日益增长的需求」，多家纱厂已提高若干品种价格。同一份共产国际通讯指出，国大党把运动重心放在抵制英货上，使其领导权落入印度资本家之手，而工人的工资与工时条件未获改善。

sources.title: International Press Correspondence, Vol.10 No.30, 26 June 1930（Virendranath Chattopadhyaya）
sources.quote: "Thanks to the movement started by Mr. Gandhi, a complete and happy change has come over in the textile industry. ... The constant demand for swadeshi cloth is mainly responsible for the now empty godowns, which had stocks worth hundreds of thousands. ... Even the calico mills which had hitherto been running double-shift have commenced working for 23 hours, and the New Commercial Mills have started double-shift to cope with the demand for cloth". ... In Bombay, the New City Mills, the Finlay Mills, the Apollo Mills and the Jacob Sassoon Mills propose to work night-shift "to meet the growing demand for Bombay mill products". The mill-owners have increased the prices of several categories of goods.
